speaker: richard_cowley
text: You have a clove in your cheek again, behind the curtain. Is the gum rising, or is the bud doing its work?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The clove is in its place, and the gown is on my back. You do not need to carry the old Roman today.

speaker: richard_cowley
text: I carried him in January when the frost was in your throat, and I have not forgotten the staff. I ask because the left cheek is rounder than the right.

speaker: john_heminges
text: If he can speak this afternoon and Navarre tomorrow, let him keep his own staff, Richard. We have enough to shift before nine without changing a principal on an hour's notice.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: Nine tomorrow is the comedy. I have the rolls by the book. Term opens, and the gowns will be in the gallery waiting on Master Kemp.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Let them wait on him. I am Navarre at two tomorrow, and I am this gown today. What is on the post across the water?

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: Crack Me at the Rose. I read it on the way up. I did not cross.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then we are not that. I have not been to their door.

speaker: richard_cowley
text: And if the cheek will not do Navarre by breakfast, I am here.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Navarre will be in his clothes at two, and at nine on the boards. Save the offer for a day when I cannot open my teeth.

speaker: john_heminges
text: The cloves have been at it since the ninth of September. That is four weeks yesterday. A shilling to a barber is cheaper than a king who mumbles his vowels at the Inns. I am not sending you. I am saying the sum.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The sum is twelve pence when it is drawn, and it is not drawn today. The Inns are coming to shout at Kemp and to ask when the king is played, not to look in my mouth.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: The king was yesterday. You were done by the middle. Today you are done in the fourth, if it goes as Monday.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Monday and today. Off in the fourth, and the book still right. Richard, stay by your own peg.

speaker: richard_cowley
text: I shall be at the foot of the stair if the clove slips.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Stay by the peg. The old Roman has the afternoon in him yet. I am not handing him over to be helpful.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Then the gown stays where it is. Nine tomorrow for the comedy. Two today for this death. Crack Me can stay on their post.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: The book has you in the fourth, and off. I have not moved the peg. I will not move it because a cheek is round.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Leave the peg. If I come off and the yard is still at it, that is the play. It is not at it for me.

speaker: richard_cowley
text: January was a throat, and a staff, and a morning's notice. This is a cheek and a clove. I can tell the two apart.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Tell them apart, and then stand still. Four weeks from the ninth, and he is speaking. That is the afternoon I want.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: You will have it. Navarre tomorrow can mind his own vowels. Today the Roman dies where he died on Monday.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: Crack Me stays their bill. I will not write it into ours, and I did not cross the water to hear it.

speaker: richard_cowley
text: Then I am at my peg, and the staff stays on its nail. I am not conning a line of him in the passage.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: On its nail. I am not generous with a part I can still say. Call me when the fourth begins, and not before.
